code:
$ mkdir app/logs
mkdir: cannot create directory 'app/logs': No such file or directory
$ mkdir -p app/logs/2026
$ ls -R app
app:
logs

app/logs:
2026
caption: Plain mkdir only makes one level; -p creates every missing parent directory in the path.

code:
$ cp app app_backup
cp: -r not specified; omitting directory 'app'
$ cp -r app app_backup
$ ls app_backup
CHANGELOG.md  logs
caption: Without -r, cp refuses to touch a directory — it only copies plain files by default.

eyebrow: mv renames and moves — same command
code:
$ mv CHANGELOG.md CHANGES.md
$ ls
CHANGES.md  app  app_backup
$ mv CHANGES.md app/
$ ls app
CHANGES.md  logs
caption: Linux has no separate rename command: mv changes where a name points, whether that's a new name or a new directory.

eyebrow: Deleting is permanent — no Recycle Bin
